meta.title: AMDL — Self-hosted Apple Music downloader
meta.description: Self-hosted Apple Music downloader saving tagged .m4a files in ALAC up to 24-bit/192 kHz, Dolby Atmos, or AAC, with web console, TUI, CLI, and MCP server.
meta.ogAlt: The AMDL headline beside three album covers, showing Apple Music on your own disk.

hero.title:
Apple Music,
on your own disk
hero.lead: Pass a link or search. AMDL downloads, decrypts, and tags tracks into **finished .m4a files on your disk** via web console, terminal UI, CLI, or MCP.
hero.shelfLabel: Made-up album covers on a shelf above a saved track file, 01. Glass Weather.m4a in ALAC 24-bit · 96 kHz.

how.title: From a link to a finished file
how.lead: AMDL resolves a link, fetches the encrypted stream, decrypts it in-process on your machine using keys from your wrapper, and pipes the audio into ffmpeg.

link.title: A link or a search
link.text: Pass a song, album, playlist, artist, or station link, or search the catalog.
link.note: Queue up to 100 links at once.

amdl.title: Inside AMDL

steps.name: Decrypt
steps.text: Runs in-process inside `amdl` with your wrapper.

steps.name: Remux
steps.text: `ffmpeg` writes `.m4a`; no decrypted whole track on disk.

steps.name: Tag
steps.text: Embeds tags, cover, and lyrics, then checks integrity.

amdl.note: If a codec fails, it falls back to the next.

file.title: Files on your disk
file.text: Songs, albums, and artists share one configurable `library/` folder tree.
file.note: Existing files are kept, not downloaded again.

how.label: Folder tree under library/ where artist folder Mira Solenne contains artist.jpg and album folder Glass Weather with numbered .m4a tracks and cover.jpg.

formats.title: Formats and codec priority
formats.lead: Download ALAC up to 24-bit / 192 kHz by default, or order a priority list of ALAC, Dolby Atmos, Dolby Digital, and AAC variants.

rows.ec3: Dolby Atmos spatial audio, if on the album.
rows.aaclc: Always tried last as fallback; not listed.

formats.caption: Order codecs in `quality_priority` (`["alac"]` by default). With `codec_alternative` on, a codec that runs out of attempts hands over to the next.

apps.title: Four ways to use one backend
apps.lead: One binary packs the CLI, MCP server, terminal UI, and backend with its web console. Use any of them, or connect the native desktop app.
apps.shown: Illustrations show the real interfaces with fictional music. The apps themselves are in English.

desktop.caption: Native app for macOS, Windows and Linux: a client of your AMDL server, or standalone with the backend inside. Its setup screen installs ffmpeg and the wrapper.
desktop.label: Desktop app album page showing Glass Weather mid-download with five of twelve tracks saved and the target library folder path.

console.caption: Served at `/console/` with nothing to install on the client. Open it across your network on port `18080` in Docker, or on this machine for a local install.
console.label: Web console Overview page with one failed link under Needs attention, three albums downloading as cards tinted in their cover colors, and one queued link.

terminal.caption: Run `amdl` with no arguments for an interactive terminal UI that shows each track's stage. For scripts, CLI subcommands write structured JSON to stdout.
terminal.label: Terminal UI showing the AMDL banner, Glass Weather downloading track by track, the command prompt, and catalog search results for Mira Solenne.

agents.caption: `amdl mcp` exposes 37 tools over stdio, from catalog search to finished download. No tool signs in, so your Apple ID password never passes through a model.
agents.label: Chat session where you ask for the new Nightjar Coast album in Dolby Atmos, and the agent calls search_catalog, start_download, and wait_for_job before reporting where the 11 tracks were saved.

chat.ask: Download the new Nightjar Coast album in Dolby Atmos.
chat.reply: Downloaded Low Tide Signals (2026) — all 11 tracks in Dolby Atmos saved to `/volume1/music/library/Nightjar Coast/Low Tide Signals/`.

agents.config: Client config printed by `amdl cli setup`

install.title: Install on your machine or in Docker
install.lead: You need an Apple Music subscription and a wrapper (the service that holds your login). Install the binary or run it in Docker.

steps.title: Install the binary
steps.text: The script verifies the download against `SHA256SUMS` and installs `amdl` into `~/.local/bin` on macOS and Linux, or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\amdl` on Windows.

steps.title: Check ffmpeg
steps.text: Every track requires `ffmpeg` 8 or later. Run `amdl doctor` to check your environment and print the command that installs anything missing.

steps.title: Install a wrapper
steps.text: `amdl wrapper install` runs it natively on Linux x86_64 and in a QEMU guest elsewhere (not Windows on ARM). Skip this if a wrapper already runs on a NAS or server.

steps.title: Start the backend service
steps.text: Starts the backend at login. `amdl service status` prints the console address; sign the wrapper in there or with `amdl wrapper login`. For a remote wrapper, pass `--wrapper <url>`.

steps.title: Get the Compose file
steps.text: In an empty directory, download the Compose file, create `data/downloads` first, and set its owner to match the container's `PUID`/`PGID` (`1000:1000` by default).

steps.title: Enable the wrapper service
steps.text: Open `docker-compose.yml` and uncomment the `wrapper-manager` service block along with the `volumes:` section at the bottom of the file.

steps.title: Start the containers
steps.text: Compose builds `wrapper-manager` from AMDL-Web's wrapper fork on first start, so the host needs internet access.

steps.title: Connect and sign in
steps.text: Open `http://localhost:18080/`, go to **Settings › Account**, set **Session service** to the address below, then save and restart from the notice.
steps.after: Sign in with your Apple ID and paste a link into **New download**. Finished files are saved to `./data/downloads`.

nas.label: NAS & ARM
nas.text: The wrapper needs Linux x86_64 with user namespaces (`unshare -Ur true` must succeed). On arm64 or a host without them like Synology DSM, use wrapper-manager v2's QEMU variant with `/dev/kvm`.

install.more: See the [install guide]({blob}/docs/install.md) and [deployment guide]({blob}/docs/deployment.md) for all options. Coming from 1.x, back up your database and read the [2.0 upgrade guide]({blob}/docs/upgrading-to-2.0.md) first.

footer.tagline: Self-hosted AGPL-3.0 tool that saves Apple Music to your own disk as .m4a files.
footer.notice: Requires your own Apple Music subscription. Each install is self-hosted for one person, with no accounts or built-in auth. Catalog reads use Apple's undocumented web-player API, which can change without notice.
